sonnet18.title: Sonnet 18
sonnet18.author: William Shakespeare
subject: Love
Beauty
Immortality
sonnet18.firstLine: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
sonnet18.excerpt:
Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate.
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
And summer's lease hath all too short a date.

daffodils.title: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud
daffodils.author: William Wordsworth
subject: Nature
Memory
Solitude
daffodils.firstLine: I wandered lonely as a cloud
daffodils.excerpt:
I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
When all at once I saw a crowd,
A host, of golden daffodils;
Beside the lake, beneath the trees,
Fluttering and dancing in the breeze.

haiku.title: An old silent pond
haiku.author: Matsuo Bashō
subject: Nature
Silence
Moment
haiku.excerpt:
An old silent pond
A frog jumps into the pond—
Splash! Silence again.

death.title: Because I could not stop for Death
death.author: Emily Dickinson
subject: Death
Immortality
Journey
death.firstLine: Because I could not stop for Death
death.excerpt:
Because I could not stop for Death—
He kindly stopped for me—
The Carriage held but just Ourselves—
And Immortality.

hope.title: Hope is the thing with feathers
hope.author: Emily Dickinson
subject: Hope
Perseverance
Nature
hope.firstLine: Hope is the thing with feathers
hope.excerpt:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul,
And sings the tune without the words,
And never stops at all.
